knowledge_answers.rationale: The wicket is broken when a bail is completely removed from the top or a stump is struck out of the ground.

Wilful post-receipt deception causes an immediate Dead-ball call and prevents either batter being dismissed from the delivery; five Penalty runs are awarded to the batting side, with specified running also retained.
No ball bars the ordinary delivery dismissals; only Hit the ball twice, Obstructing the field and Run out remain available.

Wide can be called as the ball passes; later proof of contact with the striker activates the revocation rule; any ensuing run classification must then use the contact and Leg-bye conditions rather than retain a Wide.
Wide and No ball do not count; the early Dead ball also does not count because the striker had no opportunity; only the three ordinary deliveries are valid, so six valid balls have not been reached.
